## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The `--exclude` flag needs an `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` environment-variable default. The project's CLI-flag policy requires one for every new flag, and CI sets options through the environment.

## Changes
The pull request adds a repeatable `--exclude GLOB` flag. `collect()` uses it to skip, and log, files whose basename matches any of the patterns. It also documents the flag in `docs/flags.md` and adds tests for parsing, collection and archive output.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- cli/main.py:17 — correctness — Read the `--exclude` default from `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` — When `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` is set in the environment, `--exclude` ignores it, because it uses the fixed `default=[]`. `.claude/skills/cli-flags/SKILL.md:11` says: "Every command-line flag added under `cli/` from now on must also take its default from an `ARCHIVE_<NAME>` environment variable". — CI jobs that set options through the environment cannot exclude files, so their archives still include files they meant to leave out. — Fix: In `build_parser`, build the default from `os.environ.get("ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE")` with a documented separator for multiple globs, note in `docs/flags.md` that argparse `append` adds command-line values to that default, and extend `test_exclude_defaults_to_nothing`.
